text:
Mobile outreach offers harm reduction services in Plumas County communities
W. C. Garza
The Plumas County mobile outreach program will provide harm reduction services in several local communities, according to an Aug. 19 announcement. The service includes HIV and hepatitis C testing, Naloxone distribution, safe use supplies, medical supplies, fentanyl test strips, hygiene products, wound care supplies, and additional resources.
The outreach is scheduled at various locations on specific days each month. In Portola, the mobile unit will be available in the parking lot on Commercial Street from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM on the second and fourth Mondays of each month. Greenville residents can access services at 212 Mill Street from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM on the first and third Fridays. In Twain, services are offered at Twain Store located at 130 Twain Store Road from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM on the second and fourth Fridays.
Organizers said a range of medical and safety resources will be distributed during these sessions.
Harm reduction efforts such as these are intended to support community health by providing access to essential medical supplies and information for individuals who may be at risk for infectious diseases or overdose.
Community members seeking more information about times or locations can contact local health officials or visit official county channels.
